title: Viewport: draw an arrow and the text "Operator side" at the work envelope

body:
The maintainer asked for this work, in his own words (2026-11-18):

> issue, p4, in the work envelope. there should be a Arrow "pointing" towards the user and the text stating "operator side".. so people understand where they look "into" the work envelope from.

## Problem

The viewport shows the work envelope of the machine. A user cannot tell from which side the operator looks into it. The user then does not know how the part sits, how the vise faces, or which way is "front".

## Wanted

1. The work envelope shows an arrow on the operator side. The arrow points toward the operator, away from the envelope. The text "Operator side" is next to the arrow.
2. The side comes from the machine. A 3-axis mill and a 4-axis or 5-axis machine have a default operator side (the front of the machine). A lathe, a router table, a laser or a plasma table can differ. The machine file may name the side. When it does not, a documented default for the machine type applies. A decision file in `docs/decisions/` records the defaults.
3. The arrow and the text follow the view: the text stays readable, the arrow stays at the envelope edge in 3D, and both do not hide the part or the toolpath. Draw them with the envelope, in the envelope colour or a muted one.
4. A switch hides them. Default: shown. The switch is a view setting (ephemeral UI state, no undo command). It sits with the other envelope display options.
5. The label text is plain English and is the same in all views. No G-code words.

## Constraints

- Layers: ui reads the machine data through the app API. A new machine-file field follows the machine-file rules and keeps old files valid (the field is optional).
- No per-frame work that can be cached (frame target under 10 ms). Build the arrow geometry once for each envelope change.
- A UI PR needs before and after screenshots in the PR body. Tests assert the presence, the text, the side for each machine type and the switch state, not pixel values. Update the layout test of the viewport page if it applies.
- Draw an original arrow. Use no asset from another product.

## Done means

- A test shows the arrow and the text for a mill, with the side as the default says.
- A test shows a machine file that names another side, and that an old file without the field still loads.
- A test shows that the switch hides and shows them.
- The PR has before and after screenshots.
